Q110.reason: Conduction electrons form a degenerate Fermi gas, so most sit far above kT; they are non-relativistic (v_F is about 10^6 m/s), so D is wrong.

Q111.reason: Simultaneity in O gives Δt' = -γvΔx/c², so 13 ns = γβ(10 m)/c, giving γβ = 0.39 and β ≈ 0.36.

Q112.reason: De Broglie's relation λ = h/p uses Planck's constant; the Rydberg constant and c do not enter.

Q113.reason: Electric-dipole selection rules require Δl = ±1, so 4p → 3p (Δl = 0) is forbidden, while 3d, 3s and 2s are allowed.

Q114.reason: The sign of the Hall voltage, and so the Hall coefficient, reveals whether the carriers are electrons or holes.
